title: Unified Inference: Product Hub - Overview, PRD, Design, Roadmap, Pricing, Release Notes
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This document is the product hub for the Unified Inference initiative. It consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements & acceptance criteria), high-level design specs, roadmap and themes for the next 6-12 months, pricing & packaging guidance, and the latest release notes. The intended audience is product managers, engineering leads (runtime, infra, platform), go-to-market, and customer success.

Goals and success metrics
-------------------------
- Primary goal: Provide a single, production-ready inference surface that delivers predictable latency, lower unit cost, and consistent developer experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Success metrics (12 months):
  - 99.5% of customer requests meet P95 latency SLO for targeted route classes.
  - 20% reduction in average per-token cost for mid-volume customers via Optimize recommendations.
  - 30% increase in self-serve adoption for Dedicated trials.
  - Zero customer regressions in generation quality across release rollouts (monitored via evals).

Scope (what's in / out)
-----------------------
In scope:
- Unified API surface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking.
- Model pinning, rollouts (canary/A-B), and automatic fallback policies.
- Redwood Optimize integrations: batching/caching suggestions and quantization recommendations.
- Developer experience: SDK updates, improved quickstarts, and per-route dashboards.
- Pricing & packaging: Hosted per-token/embedding rates, Dedicated reserved capacity tiers, Private licensing.

Out of scope (initial phase):
- Full multi-cloud private control plane (target: later phase).
- Deep model training / fine-tuning surfaces beyond upload-and-serve.

Key trade-offs
--------------
1. Cost vs latency: Default deployment chooses conservative batching to preserve P95 latency rather than aggressive cost-optimized batching. Optimize will recommend aggressive settings as opt-in.
2. Feature parity across deployment modes: Host-first feature set; Dedicated/Private parity achieved incrementally with clear rollout mapping.

Product requirements (PRD)
-------------------------
Functional requirements (FR):
1. FR-API-01: Single REST/SDK endpoint for inference that supports:
   - text generation and streaming responses
   - structured outputs and function/tool calling
   - embeddings and reranking
   Acceptance: API returns 200 and expected schema; streaming responses arrive within 50ms first-chunk for warm flows.
2. FR-ROUTE-01: Per-route configuration for model, SLO class (low-latency, balanced, throughput), and rollout policy.
   Acceptance: Admin console route editor stores and applies route config; route-level metrics appear in dashboard.
3. FR-FALLBACK-01: Automatic fallback to pre-configured compatible model variant on capacity pressure or failure.
   Acceptance: Fallback triggers within 150ms of determined capacity constraint and is observable in traces.
4. FR-OPT-01: Redwood Optimize recommendations surfaced per-customer with suggested batching, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles.
   Acceptance: Recommendations have an estimated cost delta and confidence score.

Non-functional requirements (NFR):
- NFR-SLO-01: P95 latency SLO by route class: low-latency <= 120ms; balanced <= 300ms; throughput <= 800ms.
- NFR-RELIABILITY-01: Platform-level uptime >= 99.9% (hosted API).
- NFR-SEC-01: Data residency controls and KMS integration for Private deployments.
- NFR-PERF-01: Support model quantization profiles and runtime kernel selection to achieve targeted cost savings (>= 15% for supported models).

Design overview (high-level)
---------------------------
1. API & Routing
   - Single public API with route definitions stored in Config Service.
   - Smart router evaluates route policy, region, customer tier, and model variants; routes to appropriate runtime pool.
   - Fallback chain defined per-route (variants by model size, quantization, region).

2. Serving runtime
   - GPU-optimized engine with kernel-selection layer, continuous batching, KV cache management, and quantization-aware execution paths.
   - Runtime exposes telemetry hooks for token-level cost/latency breakdowns.

3. Optimize integration
   - Offline analyzer consumes traces and request distributions to propose batching/caching/quantization changes.
   - UI surfaces recommendations with simulated cost/latency impact and one-click apply (for Dedicated/Hosted).

API & example request/response
-----------------------------
POST /v1/routes/{route_id}/invoke
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Body (JSON):
{
  "input": "Describe the benefits of caching for LLM inference.",
  "stream": true,
  "max_tokens": 256
}
Response streaming: first chunk must arrive within P95 target for warm flows.

Data model & telemetry
----------------------
- Traces include: request_id, route_id, model_variant, kernel_profile, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms (split by scheduling, compute, network), and cost_estimate_usd.
- Dashboard supports grouping by route, model, customer, and time window.

Rollout plan & operations
-------------------------
1. Canary (internal): 2% of traffic routed to new model/runtime config inside Redwood test org.
2. External beta: Select customers (by invite) run traffic for 1-2 weeks with active monitoring.
3. Gradual ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks at each stage.
4. Automatic rollback: Health checks evaluate generation-quality regressions (eval harness), error rates, latency SLOs.

Rollback criteria (example):
- Error rate > 1% over 5 minutes.
- P95 latency degradation > 30% compared to baseline.
- Eval regression score decrease beyond allowed delta (configured per route).

Ops runbook (high-level)
-----------------------
- On alert: Pager duty -> oncall engineer inspects route traces and runtime pool metrics.
- If fallback triggers: Confirm model variant health and scale capacity of primary pool.
- For customer-impacting incidents: Open incident in incident tracker, notify CSMs, and provide mitigation steps (route pinning, temporary config change).

Roadmap & themes (next 6-12 months)
----------------------------------
Q3 2026 (near term):
- GA of Unified API for Hosted with basic route editor and fallback support.
- Redwood Optimize: MVP recommendations and single-click apply for Hosted.
- Pricing: publish per-token updates and Dedicated reserved tiers.

Q4 2026 (mid term):
- Dedicated parity: route editor, Optimize apply, and SLA options.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdowns in dashboard and improved tracing.

Q1 2027 (longer term):
- Private deployment: VPC control plane and KMS/HSM integrations.
- Advanced Optimize: automated workload-driven quantization rollouts and regression guards.

Themes: developer-first DX, cost-aware performance, and enterprise readiness (security/SLA).

Pricing & packaging notes (guidance)
----------------------------------
- Hosted API: tiered per-token pricing. Example (guideline):
  - Standard generation: $0.0008 / input token, $0.0016 / output token
  - Embeddings: $0.00045 / unit
  - Volume discounts at > $10k/mo and committed usage discounts for larger customers.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity pricing with monthly commit and burst pricing for overage.
  - Small pool (8 GPUs): starting at $X/month (placeholder: customized per customer)
  - Enterprise bundles include extended retention for logs and premium SLA.
- Private: licensing + deployment fee + optional managed-support.
- Value-adds: Redwood Optimize Pro (chargeable add-on), advanced observability retention, and compliance packages (SOC2, HIPAA).

Release notes (v1.0.0 - GA 2026-07-01)
-------------------------------------
Highlights:
- Unified API GA for Hosted: text generation, streaming, embeddings, and reranking.
- Per-route configuration and fallback chains.
- Redwood Optimize MVP: recommendations for batching and caching.
- Dashboard: per-route latency/cost metrics and rollout controls.
Known limitations / migration notes:
- Some SDKs may require minor version bumps for streaming changes (see SDK release notes).
- Dedicated and Private feature parity pending (see roadmap above).

Appendices
----------
A. Acceptance test checklist (brief):
1. API conformance tests pass for generation and streaming.
2. Stress tests: 95th percentile routing and runtime performance within SLOs.
3. Evaluate Optimize recommendations on a representative customer workload and verify cost delta estimate within 10% of observed.

B. Sample config table (route-level)
| field | description | example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| route_id | human-readable route name | product-support-summary |
| model_variant | model + quantization | gptx-1-qa-q4-bit8 |
| slo_class | low-latency | low-latency |
| fallback_chain | ordered list of model variants | gptx-1-qa-q4-bit8, gptx-1-qa-q4-fp16 |
| cache_ttl_ms | prefix cache TTL | 60000 |

C. Links & references
- Developer quickstart: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates
- Runtime architecture: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture

If you have feedback or need a deeper design review for a specific integration (Dedicated or Private), please reach out to the product lead or open a design RFC in the product channel.
